mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% in a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are positive in more than 40% of the instances when the federal funds rate increases by more than 0.25% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in a month indicates a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending and business investment decline.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are positive in more than 60% of the instances when the unemployment rate increases by more than 0.5% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over three consecutive months signals a weakening consumer demand, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings are adversely affected.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are positive in more than 50% of the instances when RSAFS declines for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a month signals a strengthening supply side, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as increased production capacity supports economic growth.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 40% of the instances when INDPRO increases by more than 1% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3% in a month signals a strengthening labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as increased consumer confidence and spending boost corporate earnings.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 60% of the instances when UNRATE decreases by more than 0.3% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) increase by more than 5% in a month and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 1%, it signals a strong demand in the housing market coupled with accommodative monetary policy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases > 5% in 1 month and FEDFUNDS < 1%
regime_hint: early-cycle expansion with accommodative monetary policy
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 40% of the instances when HOUST increases by more than 5% and FEDFUNDS is below 1%.

mechanism_narrative: When the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in a month and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2%, it signals inflationary pressure coupled with restrictive monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% in 1 month and FEDFUNDS > 2%
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are positive in more than 50% of the instances when CPIAUCSL increases by more than 0.5% and FEDFUNDS is above 2%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals a strengthening economy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings benefit from increased economic activity.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 40% of the instances when GDPC1 increases for two consecutive quarters.
